results.raw:
When creating a URL map it’s essential to clearly distinguish between old and new destinations. Each entry should show the original address and the intended path, helping you track changes over time. This map serves as a reference but doesn’t confirm a redirect is working. Always test the old address first, then verify the final page separately. This separation ensures you catch issues early without assuming success.

Each test should focus on one redirect at a time. Use the map to note planned destinations and actual results. If a test fails, mark it as incomplete for follow-up. This approach prevents false confidence and keeps your workflow transparent.

Record every result in the map, noting any discrepancies. Consistent testing builds reliability, even when outcomes aren’t guaranteed. Stay methodical and let data guide your next steps.
